content: This medication may cause visual disturbances, such as blurred vision, seeing spots, or flashes of light, particularly when exposed to bright light. These effects are generally temporary and tend to resolve within a few days or weeks after discontinuing treatment. However, in rare cases, these vision changes may become permanent. The use of this medication can lead to a condition called ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS). In rare and severe instances, OHSS can result in the rapid accumulation of fluid in the abdominal cavity, chest, and heart regions. This condition may develop during the course of treatment or after the treatment has been stopped. Severe allergic reactions to this medication are uncommon but can occur. Symptoms of a serious allergic reaction may include rash, itching, swelling (especially of the face, tongue, or throat), severe dizziness, or difficulty breathing. If you experience any of these symptoms, seek immediate medical attention. This medication is not recommended for use during pregnancy. If you become pregnant while taking this medication, discontinue its use immediately and consult your doctor. It is not known whether this drug passes into breast milk, but it may reduce milk production. Consult your healthcare provider before breastfeeding. Clomiphene may cause dizziness or visual changes. The use of alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or engaging in activities that require alertness or clear vision until you are certain you can perform them safely. Limit the consumption of alcoholic beverages. This medication may increase the likelihood of multiple births, such as twins or triplets. Discuss the potential risks and benefits with your doctor before starting treatment. Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of this medication or increase the risk of serious side effects. It is important to maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs, as well as herbal supplements, and share this information with your doctor and pharmacist. If an overdose occurs and the individual exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). For non-emergency overdoses, contact a poison control center. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. While taking this medication, regular medical and laboratory tests, such as hormone level assessments, pelvic examinations, or ultrasounds, may be required to monitor your progress and detect any potential side effects. Ensure that you attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, contact your doctor promptly for further instructions. Do not double the dose to catch up unless directed by your healthcare provider. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Consult your pharmacist or local waste disposal company for safe disposal methods. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the medication is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information tailored to your health needs.
